stem:
Which stem in the name of an organic compound means that the longest chain has **four** carbon atoms?

*Syllabus note: Cambridge IGCSE Supplement (Extended) content; ZIMSEC O-Level.*

options.rationale: Prop- means three carbon atoms.
Pent- means five carbon atoms.
Meth 1, eth 2, prop 3, but 4.
Meth- means one carbon atom.

explanation: The stems are meth- (1), eth- (2), prop- (3), but- (4), pent- (5) and hex- (6), so but- means four carbon atoms, as in butane, C₄H₁₀.

stem: The name of a compound ends in **-ol**. To which homologous series does it belong?

options.rationale: Alkane names end in -ane.
Alkene names end in -ene.
Carboxylic acid names end in -oic acid.
The -ol ending shows an –OH group, as in ethanol.

explanation: Names ending in -ol are alcohols (methanol, ethanol, propan-1-ol). Alkanes end in -ane, alkenes in -ene and carboxylic acids in -oic acid.

stem:
Name the compound $\ce{CH3CH2CH3}$.

*Syllabus note: Cambridge IGCSE Supplement (Extended) content; ZIMSEC O-Level.*

rejected.feedback: Propene has a C=C double bond; CH₃CH₂CH₃ has only single bonds, so it is propane.
Count the carbon atoms: there are three, so the stem is prop-.

explanation: CH₃CH₂CH₃ has three carbon atoms (prop-) joined by single bonds only, so it is an alkane (-ane): propane.

stem: What is the name of $\ce{CH3COOH}$?

options.rationale: The carbon of –COOH is counted too, so there are two carbons, not one.
Two carbon atoms, including the one in –COOH.
Ethanol is CH₃CH₂OH, with an –OH group, not –COOH.
This is an ester, CH₃COOCH₃.

explanation: CH₃COOH has two carbon atoms (the –CH₃ carbon and the –COOH carbon) and the –COOH group, so it is ethanoic acid, the acid in vinegar.

stem:
Which is the structural formula of **propan-1-ol**?

*Syllabus note: Cambridge IGCSE Supplement (Extended) content; ZIMSEC O-Level.*

options.rationale: Here the –OH is on the middle carbon: this is propan-2-ol.
This is propanoic acid, with a –COOH group.
Three carbon atoms with –OH on an end carbon.
This is propane: it has no –OH group.

explanation: Propan-1-ol has a three-carbon chain (prop-) with the –OH group (-ol) on carbon 1, an end carbon: CH₃CH₂CH₂OH.

stem:
True or false: the correct name of $\ce{CH3CH2CH=CH2}$ is but-3-ene.

*Syllabus note: Cambridge IGCSE Supplement (Extended) content; ZIMSEC O-Level.*

answerSpec.feedbackTrue: It is false. Number the chain from the end nearer the double bond: the double bond starts at carbon 1, so the name is but-1-ene.
answerSpec.feedbackFalse: Correct: numbering from the end nearer the double bond gives but-1-ene.

explanation: The chain must be numbered from the end nearer the functional group. Numbered from the right, the double bond is between carbons 1 and 2, so the compound is but-1-ene.

stem:
Name the compound $\ce{CH3CH2CH2COOH}$.

*Syllabus note: Cambridge IGCSE Supplement (Extended) content; ZIMSEC O-Level.*

rejected.feedback: Count the carbon of –COOH too: there are four carbon atoms, so it is butanoic acid.
The –COOH group makes it a carboxylic acid (-oic acid), not an alcohol.

explanation: There are four carbon atoms, counting the carbon of the –COOH group, so the stem is but- and the name is butanoic acid.
hints: The carbon atom in –COOH is part of the chain.

stem:
What is the name of $\ce{CH3CH2CH(OH)CH3}$?

*Syllabus note: Cambridge IGCSE Supplement (Extended) content; ZIMSEC O-Level.*

options.rationale: This numbers the chain from the wrong end; use the end nearer the –OH group.
Four carbons; numbered from the nearer (right-hand) end, the –OH is on carbon 2.
In butan-1-ol the –OH is on an end carbon.
Count again: there are four carbon atoms in the chain.

explanation: The chain has four carbon atoms (but-) and an –OH group (-ol). Numbering from the end nearer the –OH puts it on carbon 2: butan-2-ol.
hints: Number the chain from whichever end gives the –OH group the lower number.

stem:
Name the alkene $\ce{CH2=CHCH2CH2CH3}$.

*Syllabus note: names with five or six carbon atoms are ZIMSEC O-Level content.*

rejected.feedback: Give the position of the double bond: pent-1-ene.
Number from the end nearer the double bond: pent-1-ene.
Count the carbon atoms: there are five, so the stem is pent-.

explanation: Five carbon atoms give the stem pent-; the C=C double bond starts at carbon 1 when the chain is numbered from the left, so the name is pent-1-ene.
hints: Count the carbon atoms, then number from the end nearer the double bond.

stem:
What is the name of $\ce{CH3CH2CH(CH3)CH2CH3}$?

*Syllabus note: names with five or six carbon atoms are ZIMSEC O-Level content.*

options.rationale: The longest chain has five carbons, with a methyl branch on carbon 3.
This does not use the longest chain: the ethyl group is part of a five-carbon chain.
The longest chain has five carbon atoms, not six; the sixth carbon is the branch.
Hexane has the same molecular formula, C₆H₁₄, but it is an unbranched chain.

explanation: Draw it out: the longest continuous chain has five carbon atoms (pentane) and a –CH₃ group is attached to carbon 3 (counting from either end). The name is 3-methylpentane, an isomer of hexane.
hints: Find the longest continuous chain first; the –CH₃ in brackets is a branch.

stem: Match each name with its structural formula.
explanation: Ethane CH₃CH₃ (single bond), ethene CH₂=CH₂ (double bond), ethanol CH₃CH₂OH (–OH) and ethanoic acid CH₃COOH (–COOH). CH₃COOCH₃ is the ester methyl ethanoate.

stem:
Complete the name of the ester.

*Syllabus note: Cambridge IGCSE Supplement (Extended) content; ZIMSEC O-Level.*

payload.template: The ester made from methanol and propanoic acid is called {{blank:a}} {{blank:b}}.

explanation: The alcohol part is named first with -yl (methanol → methyl); the acid part second with -oate (propanoic acid → propanoate): methyl propanoate, CH₃CH₂COOCH₃.
hints: Alcohol part first (-yl), acid part second (-oate).

stem:
Which is the structural formula of **ethyl methanoate**?

*Syllabus note: Cambridge IGCSE Supplement (Extended) content; ZIMSEC O-Level.*

options.rationale: This is methyl ethanoate: the two parts are the other way round.
Methanoate (HCOO–) from methanoic acid, joined to an ethyl group from ethanol.
This is propanoic acid, a carboxylic acid with the same molecular formula.
This is methyl methanoate: the alcohol part has only one carbon.

explanation: Ethyl methanoate is made from ethanol (ethyl, –CH₂CH₃) and methanoic acid (methanoate, HCOO–). The acid part is written first in the formula: HCOOCH₂CH₃.
hints: The -oate part comes from the acid and is written first in the formula.

stem:
Tatenda is given the names of three organic compounds: **but-1-ene**, **methyl ethanoate** and **butane**.

*Syllabus note: Cambridge IGCSE Supplement (Extended) content; ZIMSEC O-Level.*

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: To which homologous series does but-1-ene belong?

options.rationale: The -ene ending shows a C=C double bond.
Alkane names end in -ane.
Alcohol names end in -ol.
Ester names have two words, such as methyl ethanoate.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Write the structural formula of but-1-ene.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: How many carbon atoms are there in one molecule of methyl ethanoate?

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Methyl ethanoate is made from an alcohol and a carboxylic acid.

parts.label: (i)
parts.stem: Name the alcohol.

rejected.feedback: The alcohol gives the first word: methyl comes from methanol.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.stem: Name the carboxylic acid.

rejected.feedback: The acid gives the second word: ethanoate comes from ethanoic acid.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Explain why the name **butene** is not enough to identify a single compound.

points.description: The double bond can be in different positions in the four-carbon chain (between C1 and C2, or between C2 and C3)
These are different compounds (but-1-ene and but-2-ene), so a position number is needed

parts.explanation: In a four-carbon chain the C=C double bond can start at carbon 1 (but-1-ene) or at carbon 2 (but-2-ene). These are different compounds with the same molecular formula, C₄H₈, so the position number must be given.

explanation: But-1-ene is an alkene, CH₂=CHCH₂CH₃. Methyl ethanoate, CH₃COOCH₃, has three carbon atoms and is made from methanol and ethanoic acid. 'Butene' could mean but-1-ene or but-2-ene, so the position of the double bond must be stated.
workedSolution:
1. (a) -ene: alkene.
2. (b) but- = 4 carbons; -1-ene: C=C between C1 and C2: CH₂=CHCH₂CH₃.
3. (c) CH₃COOCH₃: 2 carbons from the ethanoate part + 1 from the methyl part = 3.
4. (d) methyl ← methanol; ethanoate ← ethanoic acid.
5. (e) The double bond could be at position 1 or 2: two different compounds.
hints: For an ester, the first word comes from the alcohol and the second from the acid.

stem:
This question is about compounds with six carbon atoms.

*Syllabus note: names with five or six carbon atoms are ZIMSEC O-Level content.*

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Name the unbranched alkane $\ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH2CH3}$.

rejected.feedback: There is no double bond, so the ending is -ane.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Name the compound $\ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH2COOH}$.

rejected.feedback: Count the carbon in –COOH as well: six carbon atoms.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Name the compound $\ce{CH3CH=CHCH2CH2CH3}$.

rejected.feedback: Number from the end nearer the double bond.
Give the position of the double bond.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Give the molecular formula of hexan-1-ol.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Which of the compounds in (a) to (d) is **unsaturated**?

options.rationale: Hexane has only single bonds.
The C=O of the –COOH group is not a carbon–carbon double bond.
Hexan-1-ol has only single bonds between its carbon atoms.
It has a C=C double bond.

explanation: (a) Six carbons, single bonds: hexane. (b) Six carbons including the –COOH carbon: hexanoic acid. (c) Six carbons with C=C starting at carbon 2 (numbered from the left): hex-2-ene, which is unsaturated. (d) Hexan-1-ol is C₆H₁₃OH, molecular formula C₆H₁₄O.
workedSolution:
1. (a) hex- + -ane: hexane.
2. (b) 5 carbons in the chain + 1 in –COOH = 6: hexanoic acid.
3. (c) Numbering from the left, the double bond starts at C2: hex-2-ene.
4. (d) CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH with n = 6: C₆H₁₃OH = C₆H₁₄O.
5. (e) Only (c) has a C=C double bond.
hints: Hex- means six carbon atoms; count the –COOH carbon in (b).

stem: Displayed formulae show every atom and every bond.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Draw the displayed formula of ethanol.

points.description: Two carbon atoms joined by a single bond, five hydrogen atoms, each carbon with four bonds
–O–H drawn with the O–H bond shown, oxygen bonded to a carbon atom

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Draw the displayed formula of ethanoic acid.

points.description: A CH₃ group (three C–H bonds) bonded to the carboxyl carbon
Carboxyl carbon with C=O double bond and C–O–H, with the O–H bond shown

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: How many covalent bonds (shared pairs of electrons) are there in a molecule of ethene? Count the C=C double bond as two bonds.

options.rationale: Four C–H bonds plus the C=C double bond counted as two: 4 + 2 = 6.
This counts the double bond as one bond.
This counts only the C–H bonds.
Each hydrogen forms one bond and each carbon four; there are 6 bonds in total.

explanation: Ethanol: CH₃–CH₂–O–H with every C–H, C–C, C–O and O–H bond drawn. Ethanoic acid: CH₃– attached to a carbon that has a C=O and an O–H group. Ethene has four C–H bonds and one C=C double bond (two shared pairs), six bonds in all.
workedSolution:
1. (a) H₃C–CH₂–O–H drawn out: 5 C–H, 1 C–C, 1 C–O, 1 O–H.
2. (b) H₃C–C(=O)–O–H drawn out.
3. (c) Ethene: 4 C–H + C=C (2) = 6.
hints: Every carbon must end up with four bonds; draw the O–H bond as a line.

stem: Which of these compounds is an **alkene**?

options.rationale: The -ane ending shows an alkane.
The -ol ending shows an alcohol.
The -ene ending shows a C=C double bond.
The -oic acid ending shows a carboxylic acid.

explanation: Alkene names end in -ene. Propene, CH₃CH=CH₂, is the alkene with three carbon atoms.

stem:
True or false: each molecule of propanoic acid contains three carbon atoms.

*Syllabus note: Cambridge IGCSE Supplement (Extended) content; ZIMSEC O-Level.*

answerSpec.feedbackTrue: Correct: CH₃CH₂COOH has three carbon atoms, including the one in –COOH.
answerSpec.feedbackFalse: It is true. Prop- means three carbon atoms, and the carbon of –COOH is one of them: CH₃CH₂COOH.

explanation: The stem prop- means a chain of three carbon atoms; in a carboxylic acid the –COOH carbon is counted in the chain, so propanoic acid is CH₃CH₂COOH.

stem:
A fruity-smelling ester has the structural formula $\ce{CH3CH2COOCH2CH2CH3}$. (Aᵣ: H = 1, C = 12, O = 16)

*Syllabus note: Cambridge IGCSE Supplement (Extended) content; ZIMSEC O-Level.*

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Name the ester.

rejected.feedback: The alcohol part (propyl) comes first and the acid part (propanoate) second; here both are three carbons long.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Name the alcohol from which it is made.

rejected.feedback: The –CH₂CH₂CH₃ group is joined through its end carbon, so the alcohol is propan-1-ol.
Give the position of the –OH group: propan-1-ol.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Name the carboxylic acid from which it is made.

rejected.feedback: CH₃CH₂COO– has three carbon atoms: propanoate, from propanoic acid.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Give the molecular formula of the ester.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Calculate the relative molecular mass of the ester.

explanation: CH₃CH₂COO– is the propanoate part (three carbons, from propanoic acid) and –CH₂CH₂CH₃ is the propyl part (from propan-1-ol), so the ester is propyl propanoate. It has 6 C, 12 H and 2 O atoms: C₆H₁₂O₂, Mᵣ = 6 × 12 + 12 × 1 + 2 × 16 = 116.
workedSolution:
1. Split the formula at –COO–: CH₃CH₂COO– | –CH₂CH₂CH₃.
2. Acid part: 3 carbons → propanoate (propanoic acid). Alcohol part: 3 carbons on an end carbon → propyl (propan-1-ol).
3. Name: propyl propanoate.
4. Count atoms: C 3 + 3 = 6; H 5 + 7 = 12; O 2 → C₆H₁₂O₂.
5. Mᵣ = 72 + 12 + 32 = 116.
hints: Split the ester at –COO–: the part with C=O comes from the acid.
In propyl propanoate both parts happen to have three carbons.

stem:
What is the name of $\ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2COOH}$?

*Syllabus note: names with five or six carbon atoms are ZIMSEC O-Level content.*

options.rationale: This leaves out the carbon atom of the –COOH group.
The –COOH group makes it a carboxylic acid, not an alcohol.
Count again: there are five carbon atoms, not six.
Five carbon atoms, counting the one in –COOH.

explanation: There are four carbon atoms in CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂– and one more in –COOH: five in total, so the name is pentanoic acid.
hints: Count the –COOH carbon as part of the chain.
